title: Cauchy Reduction of the Discriminant Route to S₅ for X⁵ − X − 1
description: A machine-verified strengthening of the discriminant-route assembler for Gal(X⁵−X−1/ℚ) ≅ S₅ (sibling: abel-ruffini-oq-07-discriminant). That route takes 'Gal contains a 3-cycle' as a hypothesis; classically the 3-cycle is not exhibited explicitly but extracted from the divisibility 3 ∣ |Gal| via Cauchy's theorem. This entry supplies the missing combinatorial bridge isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three: on at most 5 points, every permutation of order 3 is automatically a 3-cycle (there is no room for two disjoint 3-cycles), proven from the cycle-type calculus (each cycle length divides orderOf g = 3 and is ≥ 2, hence = 3; the support bound 3k ≤ 5 with g ≠ 1 forces a single 3-cycle). Combining it with Cauchy (exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card) gives gal_eq_top_of_three_dvd_card_transitive_odd: a transitive G ≤ S₅ with 3 ∣ |G| and ANY odd permutation equals ⊤ — the classical Selmer criterion in its sharpest form, with the 3-cycle now produced internally. Everything is fully machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms (only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no native_decide).

meta.author: Selmer (1956); Jordan (1873); Cauchy (1845)
meta.assumptions: This file strengthens the discriminant-route reduction of Gal(X⁵−X−1) ≅ S₅ by discharging its 3-cycle hypothesis via Cauchy's theorem. The combinatorial bridge isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three (on ≤ 5 points, order 3 ⟹ 3-cycle) is unconditional and uses only Mathlib's cycle-type API. The final assembler gal_eq_top_of_three_dvd_card_transitive_odd takes two hypotheses: (i) the Galois action is transitive on the 5 roots (from irreducibility, Selmer 1956); (ii) Gal contains an odd permutation (from Δ = 2869 not being a square) — and the divisibility datum 3 ∣ |Gal|, from which Cauchy internally produces the order-3 element. It concludes Gal = ⊤ = S₅. These inputs are explicit HYPOTHESES, not axioms: the bridges that produce '3 ∣ |Gal|', transitivity, and the odd permutation in full generality (Dedekind–Frobenius cycle types; the discriminant criterion 'Gal ⊆ A_n ⟺ disc is a square') are not present in Mathlib v4.26.0. Every theorem is fully machine-checked with 0 sorries and 0 axioms (only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no native_decide, so no Lean.ofReduceBool).

overview.historicalContext: Galois (1831) reduced solvability by radicals to solvability of a polynomial's permutation group, and X⁵ − X − 1 (irreducible by Selmer 1956) is a standard unsolvable witness with Galois group S₅. Two routes pin S₅ down: the discriminant (Gal ⊆ A_n iff disc is a square) and Jordan's 1873 theorem (primitive + 3-cycle ⟹ ⊇ alternating). The sibling entry assembles these from a 3-cycle taken as given; but a 3-cycle is classically obtained not by exhibiting a permutation, only from the divisibility 3 ∣ |Gal| and Cauchy's 1845 theorem. The last combinatorial step — that an order-3 element of S₅ must be a 3-cycle — is the small fact this entry formalizes and uses to close the gap.
overview.problemStatement: Strengthen the discriminant-route reduction Gal(X⁵−X−1) ≅ S₅ by replacing the explicit '3-cycle in Gal' hypothesis with the weaker, classically-available divisibility 3 ∣ |Gal|, extracting the 3-cycle internally via Cauchy's theorem.
overview.text: This entry machine-verifies, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the combinatorial bridge isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three (on at most 5 points, order 3 forces a 3-cycle) and uses it to reduce the discriminant assembler's hypotheses. The final theorem gal_eq_top_of_three_dvd_card_transitive_odd states that a transitive subgroup G ≤ S₅ with 3 ∣ |G| and containing some odd permutation equals all of S₅, with the order-3 (hence 3-cycle) element produced by Cauchy's theorem rather than supplied by hand.
overview.proofStrategy: Work in S₅ = Equiv.Perm (Fin 5). (1) Bridge: for g with orderOf g = 3, every entry n of cycleType g divides lcm(cycleType g) = orderOf g = 3 (lcm_cycleType) and satisfies 2 ≤ n (two_le_of_mem_cycleType), so n = 3; hence cycleType g = replicate k 3. The sum of the cycle type is 3k and is ≤ card α ≤ 5 (sum_cycleType_le), while g ≠ 1 gives k ≥ 1 (card_cycleType_pos); thus k = 1 and cycleType g = {3}, i.e. g.IsThreeCycle. (2) Assembler over order: feed the bridge into the prime-degree/Jordan/index-2 argument to weaken IsThreeCycle to orderOf g = 3. (3) Cauchy: from 3 ∣ |G|, exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card yields x : G with orderOf x = 3; transfer the order to the ambient group via Subgroup.orderOf_coe and apply the order-based assembler.
keyInsights: On fewer than 6 points there is no room for two disjoint 3-cycles, so an order-3 permutation is forced to be a single 3-cycle — the small combinatorial fact that lets Cauchy's element double as Jordan's 3-cycle.
lcm(cycleType) = orderOf and sum(cycleType) = |support| together turn 'order 3 on ≤ 5 points' into a one-line constraint: parts all 3, total ≤ 5, nonempty ⟹ exactly one part.

The divisibility 3 ∣ |Gal| is the genuinely available number-theoretic datum (it is unconditional for X⁵ − X − 1); exhibiting an explicit 3-cycle is not, so routing through Cauchy is the faithful formalization.
The reduction excludes the Frobenius group F₂₀ (order 20, no element of order 3) directly: 3 ∣ |G| is exactly what fails for F₂₀, leaving S₅ as the only transitive option with an odd element.

sections.title: Statement and the Cauchy Reduction
sections.summary: Documents the goal: discharge the '3-cycle in Gal' hypothesis of the sibling discriminant entry via Cauchy's theorem plus the fact that on ≤ 5 points an order-3 permutation is a 3-cycle. Lists the three machine-checked results and the still-open number-theoretic bridges.
sections.mathContext: Classically a 3-cycle in Gal comes from 3 ∣ |Gal| (Cauchy) plus 'order 3 ⟹ 3-cycle on 5 points', not from an explicit permutation.

sections.title: The Combinatorial Bridge: order 3 ⟹ 3-cycle
sections.summary: isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three: on a finite type of cardinality ≤ 5, orderOf g = 3 implies g.IsThreeCycle. Each cycle length divides orderOf g = 3 and is ≥ 2, hence equals 3, so cycleType g = replicate k 3; the support bound 3k ≤ 5 together with g ≠ 1 forces k = 1, i.e. cycleType g = {3}.
sections.mathContext: lcm(cycleType g) = orderOf g = 3 ⟹ parts ∈ {3}; sum(cycleType g) = |support| ≤ 5 ⟹ at most one part; g ≠ 1 ⟹ at least one part.

sections.title: The Strengthened Assemblers
sections.summary: gal_eq_top_of_transitive_orderThree_odd weakens the 3-cycle hypothesis to orderOf g = 3 (via the bridge), routing through prime-degree primitivity, Jordan's theorem and index-2 maximality of A₅. gal_eq_top_of_three_dvd_card_transitive_odd then extracts the order-3 element from 3 ∣ |G| via Cauchy (exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card), transferring its order with Subgroup.orderOf_coe.
sections.mathContext: Cauchy: prime p ∣ |G| ⟹ ∃ element of order p; here p = 3, and on Fin 5 that element is a 3-cycle, so Jordan applies.

mainTheorems.name: isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three
mainTheorems.description: On a finite type of cardinality at most 5, every permutation of order 3 is a 3-cycle. Proven from the cycle-type calculus: parts divide orderOf g = 3 and are ≥ 2 hence = 3, and the support bound 3k ≤ 5 with g ≠ 1 forces a single part. The reusable bridge classically taken for granted when passing from '3 ∣ |Gal|' to 'a 3-cycle in Gal'.

mainTheorems.name: gal_eq_top_of_three_dvd_card_transitive_odd
mainTheorems.description: The Selmer criterion in its sharpest verified form: a transitive subgroup G ≤ S₅ with 3 ∣ |G| and containing some odd permutation equals all of S₅. The order-3 (hence 3-cycle) element is extracted internally by Cauchy's theorem, so only transitivity, 3 ∣ |G|, and an odd permutation remain as hypotheses.

mainTheorems.name: gal_eq_top_of_transitive_orderThree_odd
mainTheorems.description: The discriminant-route assembler with the 3-cycle hypothesis weakened to orderOf g = 3, via isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three, prime-degree primitivity, Jordan's theorem and index-2 maximality of A₅.

mainTheorems.name: card_fin5_prime
mainTheorems.description: The degree Nat.card (Fin 5) = 5 is prime — the structural hypothesis that upgrades the transitive Galois action to a primitive one, enabling Jordan's theorem.

conclusion.summary: This entry machine-verifies, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, the combinatorial bridge that on at most 5 points an order-3 permutation is a 3-cycle, and uses it together with Cauchy's theorem to strengthen the discriminant-route reduction of Gal(X⁵−X−1/ℚ) = S₅. The final assembler needs only transitivity, 3 ∣ |Gal|, and some odd permutation — the genuinely available classical data — rather than an explicitly exhibited 3-cycle.
conclusion.implications:
1. Faithful reduction: 3 ∣ |Gal| (not an explicit 3-cycle) is the datum the Selmer/discriminant argument actually supplies; routing through Cauchy makes the formalization match the textbook proof.

2. Reusable lemma: isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three is a clean, self-contained group-theory fact useful for any prime-degree-5 Galois argument or small-symmetric-group analysis.

3. Sharper assembler: gal_eq_top_of_three_dvd_card_transitive_odd packages the entire group-theoretic content of the discriminant route into a single theorem consuming only divisibility and parity data.

4. Honest axiom accounting: the remaining hypotheses isolate exactly the number-theoretic bridges still absent from Mathlib (Dedekind–Frobenius cycle types and the discriminant criterion), keeping the file axiom-free.
openQuestions: Discharge the '3 ∣ |Gal|' hypothesis by formalizing that the Galois group of an irreducible quintic with the right modular factorization contains an element of order 3 (Dedekind–Frobenius at a suitable prime).

Generalize isThreeCycle_of_orderOf_eq_three to: on a type of cardinality < 2p, an element of prime order p is a single p-cycle — the natural statement behind 'prime order ⟹ cycle' in small symmetric groups.
Combine this assembler with a formal discriminant criterion (Gal ⊆ A_n ⟺ disc a square) so that disc_not_square from the sibling entry discharges the odd-permutation hypothesis automatically.

crossReferences.description: The sibling discriminant entry proves the assembler 'transitive + 3-cycle + odd ⟹ S₅' with the 3-cycle taken as a hypothesis. This entry discharges that hypothesis: on ≤ 5 points order 3 forces a 3-cycle, and Cauchy's theorem supplies the order-3 element from 3 ∣ |Gal|, yielding the sharper criterion that needs only 3 ∣ |G| and an odd permutation.

The original OQ-07 entry uses a distinguished transposition (the cube of the order-6 Frobenius at p=2). This entry instead routes through Cauchy and Jordan, consuming the divisibility 3 ∣ |Gal| and any odd permutation.
A second concrete Abel–Ruffini witness quintic, X⁵−X−1, unsolvable by radicals because (modulo the modular inputs) its Galois group is S₅.

references.citation: Selmer, E. S. (1956). 'On the irreducibility of certain trinomials.' Mathematica Scandinavica 4, 287-302. Proves Xⁿ − X − 1 irreducible over ℚ for all n.
Jordan, C. (1873). Sur la limite de transitivité des groupes non alternés. Establishes that a primitive permutation group containing a 3-cycle contains the alternating group.
Dummit, D. S. and Foote, R. M., Abstract Algebra (3rd ed.), Wiley (2004). Section 14.6–14.8: discriminant criterion and Galois groups of quintics; Cauchy's theorem in Section 3.
